summary: Internal refactor: CAD, the sketch solver bridge, the kernel bridge, CAM, the output audit, DXF and G-code imports, sketch snaps, dimension placement and simulation now read every tolerance from one named precision policy in src/domain/precision/cadPrecision.ts. The policy names each tolerance by its role, states its unit and meaning, and exports CAD_PRECISION_VERSION = 1. Places that used the same value for different reasons get separate roles. Kernel confusion, the smallest model length, the CAD to CAM endpoint, simulation clearance and machine geometry are all 1e-7 and stay separate. The solver's collapsed start, the gear undercut slack, the gear bound reserve, snap tangency and the G-code R arc chord are all 1e-12 and stay separate. In sketch geometry, size refusals read the smallest model length and boundary contacts read kernel confusion; the gear's radial root reads the smallest model length. Size-based tolerances become policy functions: cadRoundoff for ulps of a magnitude, cadClosureTolerance for analytic closure, cadSupportedLength for a length within the minimum length and the 1e6 mm model extent, and cadOutputFitting for the output audit's allowances. Each replaces an expression of the same form and gives the same bits. The survey found 434 candidate literals in non-test source. 246 moved behind 59 roles and the policy functions (58 are read directly or through a policy function; the drag floor mirrors the Rust solver). 188 stay, each with its reason: view and pointer space that never reaches model coordinates, unit factors, the 1e9 coordinate budget, product limits and defaults, help text, comments, fixtures and benchmarks. Sketch snap intersections and dimension placement write sketch coordinates and saved placements, so their tolerances are roles rather than view-space exemptions. docs/maintainers/precision-survey.md lists every candidate. A new test checks the ordering between roles, pins this version's values, checks each policy function against the expression it replaces, pins the closure crossovers, and checks that the Rust solver's acceptance, closure multiplier and drag constants agree with the policy. Boundary tests for 39 roles put one input just inside and one just outside each threshold, through the code that reads the role. gearJoinPerModule has none, because no valid gear reaches its threshold. Three relations that ought to hold do not, and are recorded as known rather than changed. First, the solver accepts residuals of 1e-10 mm, while structural checks hold arc endpoints to closure, which is 1e-12 mm up to about 563 mm and below 1e-10 mm up to about 56,295 mm. Second, closure grows past kernel confusion and the CAD to CAM endpoint above about 5.6e7 mm, although sketch coordinates are accepted up to 1e9 mm. Third, closure passes the CAM coincidence of 1e-9 mm above about 562,950 mm, inside the 1e6 mm model extent. A square near x = 999,000 mm with a 1.5134e-9 mm closing gap is closed in CAD but rejected by the CAM handoff. Tests reproduce the second and third. Imported STEP shape tolerances and UPID planning tolerances are still adopted as they were, and are now documented. The Rust solver names its closure multiplier CLOSURE_ULPS in both places that used it; the compiled module is byte-identical. npm run lint also runs a check that flags new tolerances outside the policy module in any spelling: negative exponents, small decimals, powers of ten, numbers parsed from strings, and Number.EPSILON through any access. A per-file list records the literals that stay. A maintainer page, docs/maintainers/precision.md, lists the roles, the ordering and how to add a role.
warning: No breaking change for installed posts, machine packages, saved revisions, CAD files, agents or controller output. Every moved tolerance keeps its value and its comparison, so geometry, snaps, dimension placement, CAM plans and controller output are bit-identical. No new refusal is added, and NaN handling is unchanged: cadSupportedLength replaces only checks that already had its exact form. The worker protocol and the committed WebAssembly module are unchanged; the Rust source only names an existing constant.

checklist.schema: No CAD, sketch graph, UPID, post, machine package, execution plan, saved revision, storage, journal, worker reply or native buffer protocol schema change. Sketch annotation placement ranges read the model extent (1e6) and annotationMinimumRadiusMm (1e-6) where they wrote those values. The native protocol stays version 7. The Rust source names its closure multiplier CLOSURE_ULPS (8.0) in both places that used it, with the same line count; solver:build leaves the committed WebAssembly module byte-identical. Post engine API remains 1 and saved-job engine remains 3. CAD_PRECISION_VERSION is new and is not yet stored anywhere.
checklist.events: No execution event, input-version, cancellation or WebMCP behaviour change. Reading a role is a property read on a frozen object, and the policy functions are the expressions they replace.
checklist.capabilities: No post or machine capability change, and no WebMCP tool added, removed or changed. No UI control or user-visible text changes.
checklist.auditAndOutput: No generation, audit, numbering, encoding, line ending, feed or controller-file change. The output audit's point, length and arc sweep allowances come from cadOutputFitting with the same values; UPID planning tolerances from documents are still used as before. Known and not changed: the audit's rounding guard is a fixed epsilon. With a plan endpoint tolerance of 0, which DXF imports use, it rejects some correctly rounded half-way coordinates from 8 mm up. For example, a planned X 8.0015 that a three-decimal post emits as 8.002 fails with POST_AUDIT_MOTION_MISMATCH. The guard had this value before this release, and a fix belongs in a separate change.
checklist.installationAndStorage: No installed package, revision, browser-cache or folder storage change.
checklist.verification: Identical output, each comparison on a snapshot of 8c7c3b50 and on this branch: the post conformance report for robofil-100-v2 is byte-identical, and the UPID conformance report differs only in the absolute file paths it names. One scratch script took both repository DXF files through parse, conversion to UPID, a reviewed start and controller compensation, the execution plan (81 and 13 events) and the robofil-100-v2 post with the properties of each of its three fixtures, including the post runtime's output audit. It also took the two ISO evidence programs through G-code parse, structure, contours and preview. Both reports are 485,866 bytes and identical. A second scratch script covered the code review round 1 touched: gears at and just below the undercut limit, sketch sizes at the minimum length and model extent, squares near the CAM endpoint and coincidence through the CAM handoff, 120 snap queries each run four ways (including the review's tangent snap at (5, 6.0000000000002)), dimension layout, moves and placement, and external G-code R arcs with ends 0 to 1e-3 mm apart. Both reports are 10,698,021 bytes and identical. The sketch equation baseline (5,131 inputs), relation baseline, 0.0.757 native baseline, frozen PlaneGCS corpus, released piece snapshots, controller output and controller program suites pass unchanged. Tests touched: none; vitest.config.ts adds src/domain/precision to the pure-domain project. New: cadPrecision.test.ts, 22 tests: the version 1 values and freezing, 13 ordering relations that hold and 3 known violations that must stay violated, the closure crossovers from both sides, reproducers for known violations 2 and 3 through the CAD to CAM handoff, each policy function against the expression it replaces, and agreement with the Rust solver's ACCEPT_MM, ACCEPT_RADIANS, CLOSURE_ULPS and drag reached floor, with both closure expressions pinned. precisionLiteralScan.test.ts, 3 tests: 17 spellings found on their lines, 7 lines that must pass, and a clean repository scan. Boundary tests: 28 *.boundaries.test.ts files with 85 tests put literal inputs just inside and just outside the thresholds of 39 roles, through the code that reads them. That code is snaps, dimension placement, sketch input, the native solver, gears, the OpenCascade kernel, the CAD to CAM handoff, planning, UPID validation, the output audit, DXF and G-code imports, and simulation. gearJoinPerModule is skipped: a search over valid gears found join gaps of at most about 1e-9 × module, a tenth of its threshold. Swapping two roles fails an ordering relation each time: handoff endpoint and coincidence, closure floor and solver residual, approximation chord and tessellation, angular accuracy and kernel direction. Each of the six Rust mutants of the closure expressions, including 8 to 16 in the row tolerance, fails the agreement test. Multiplying each role by 10 in turn, against the tests related to its readers with the precision tests excluded, 57 of the 58 roles read directly or through a policy function now fail at least one test. A re-run of the 39 roles that the new boundary tests cover shows that each now fails its boundary test; before them, 18 roles were caught and these 39 only by the version pin. The others keep their round 0 and round 1 results. Not caught: gearJoinPerModule, whose threshold no valid gear can reach. The drag floor has no TypeScript reader and only the Rust agreement test covers it. Each of the 39 roles also fails its boundary files at ×0.1, and all 85 boundary tests pass at ×1. Related tests are found through imports, and no e2e spec ran under the mutations. Checks after the boundary tests: full Vitest, 603 files and 6,848 tests passed (575 and 6,763 before them, 573 and 6,738 at 8c7c3b50); tsc -b passed with the new tests; npm run lint passed with zero oxlint findings and the precision literal check over 595 files; check-release passed on its own, and against origin/main fails only on the expected version gap (main 0.0.789, this record follows 0.0.790). The boundary tests add only test files, so the review round 1 results stand: npm run build including docs:check, ui:check, solver:build with no diff and solver:check with a byte-identical module, post:conformance and upid:conformance, and the e2e specs cad-sketch-constraints 28/28, cad-workflow 32/32 and gcode-inspection 2/2, each alone with 2 workers (dxf-import-units 3/3 and machine-package-install 2/2 in round 0). There is no machine verification.
